Taylorville Memorial Hospital

Taylorville Memorial Hospital, a 25-bed critical access hospital in Memorial Health's five-hospital system, has a new CEO and a system-wide EHR migration underway — scroll down for the live, wired-up Taylorville + Vorro pipeline

Where a system-wide EHR migration meets a new CEO's open mandate
$105MEHR consolidation project underway across Memorial Health's five hospitals — moving from Oracle Health (Cerner) and TruBridge (formerly CPSI) to Epic, with a Q1 2027 "big bang" go-live
Taylorville Memorial Hospital is a real, operating 25-bed critical access hospital (est. 1906), part of Memorial Health's five-hospital system based in Springfield, IL. Aaron Puchbauer became President & CEO in March 2026, replacing a retiring predecessor, and was reported as explicitly tasked with exploring new ways to meet patient needs. In the same window, Memorial Health is running a $105M system-wide project consolidating three EHR platforms (Oracle Health/Cerner, TruBridge/CPSI, and Altera's TouchWorks in clinics) onto Epic, with implementation starting around September 2026 and a Q1 2027 go-live. A hospital moving its entire EHR foundation is exactly the moment a connector layer matters most — keeping the non-EHR systems around it (payer, clearinghouse, ancillary) connected through the transition instead of each needing its own migration project.

The Integration Pitch

Why Vorro, why Taylorville Memorial Hospital, why now

Taylorville Memorial is a small, real critical access hospital inside a health system mid-transition: Memorial Health's $105M move from Cerner and TruBridge onto Epic is underway right now, with a Q1 2027 go-live. A new CEO arrived in March 2026 with an explicit mandate to explore new approaches. Vorro's role in a moment like this isn't to compete with the EHR migration — it's to keep the payer, clearinghouse and ancillary connections around the EHR intact while the foundation underneath changes.

The highest-leverage moment is now, during the migration's implementation phase (started ~Sept 2026, live Q1 2027) — before new point-to-point integrations get built against the old systems and have to be redone against Epic.

Not a competing EHR project; the connective tissue around it. The Epic migration and clinical workflow stay Memorial Health's; the non-EHR system connections that need to survive the transition are what Vorro would help carry through.
